sections.heading: Academic Background, Mission & Vision
sections.content_html:
Academic Background, Mission & Vision

I am a Computer, Data, and Information Scientist and Educator, currently serving as an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at Texas Woman’s University (TWU) and the Principal Investigator on an active $600K collaborative National Science Foundation (NSF) grant. My academic trajectory was shaped by systematic, rigorous training in Mathematics, Systems Engineering, and Computer & Information Science across Egypt and leading United States institutions. It was further refined through doctoral and postdoctoral research at the University of Texas at Austin (UT Austin) and the University of Arkansas at Little Rock (UA Little Rock), where I earned my Ph.D. in Computer and Information Science, and anchored by enterprise industry experience at global technology leaders including Intel and AbbVie.

I am dedicated to advancing leadership in critical and emerging technologies. My work at the intersection of AI and the Life Sciences addresses high-priority goals in public health, computational biosecurity, and biomedical foundation models. By developing transparent, interpretable, and ethical AI frameworks, I provide the foundational computational tools necessary to collaborate and lead in global biotechnology.

Information Science fundamentally unites computer science, data science, library science, psychology, and cognitive ergonomics. Originating from an Electrical and Computer Engineering background, I was drawn to this interdisciplinary synthesis to understand how complex data architectures interact with real-world users and biomedical discovery pipelines. My doctoral and ongoing investigations bridge automated data integration, entity resolution, and knowledge discovery—uniting graph theory, machine learning, and natural language processing to resolve ambiguity, optimize modularity, and extract truth from complex, disparate data sources.

My research group investigates data quality within foundation models, specifically as it applies to proteomics, structural biology, drug discovery, and biomedical knowledge discovery. Our multimodal neuro-symbolic methodology harmonizes classical statistical rigor (Bayesian frameworks, Markovian transition matrices) with contemporary architectures like Graph Neural Networks and Transformers to ensure both high predictive accuracy and physical interpretability.

My career is anchored in service, integrity, and inclusive mentorship. My commitment to academic excellence ensures that the next generation of scientists is equipped to solve the most complex computational challenges of the 21st century. I mentor emerging researchers through a collaborative, guild-based apprenticeship model that prioritizes technical mastery and underrepresented voices in computational science. Beyond the laboratory, I contribute to community-building initiatives and public discourse on national, international, and cyber security, while providing technical advisory across end-to-end data science lifecycles. I find balance through civic, social, and spiritual engagement—whether through community leadership, Islamic scholarship, hiking, creative writing, or visiting historical archives.

Currently, I am working on a new theoretical AI architecture to bridge the gap in my publications, ensuring my research contributions span both fundamental theory and applied computational sciences.

Mission

To advance scientific discovery by fostering an accessible, ethical, and artificially intelligent data ecosystem. Driving automatic integration of scientific information, ensuring responsible and sustainable scientific computing, and empowering underrepresented groups in computational and data sciences through collaborative guild mentorship.

Vision

A future where data quality, graph theory, and foundation models unite into transparent, ethical systems that accelerate biomedical discovery. To define the next generation of biomedical intelligence where structured relational networks clarify the underlying logic of life.

Core Competencies

Artificial Intelligence (AI) Language Modeling Data Engineering High Performance Computing (HPC) Human Computer Interaction Information Retrieval Network Biology Biomedical Informatics AI for Life Sciences Graphics Visualization Eye Tracking Information Seeking Graph Theory Graph Databases & Knowledge Graphs Network Science Data Quality Natural Language Processing GPU Programming Graph Neural Networks Data Integration C++ Python TensorFlow PyTorch Unity HTML JavaScript OpenGL MySQL SQL Server Google Cloud MVC Java Spring SQL Hibernate Oracle PL/SQL ETL & OLAP webMethods BSCS C# / .NET Virtual Reality (VR) CAVE Systems CUDA WebGL SLAM 3D Reconstruction

News & Announcements

October 2025

Awarded a $600,000 ($210,000 TWU portion) collaborative National Science Foundation (NSF CISE/CCF) grant as Principal Investigator for "Towards auto-prompt textual annotations generation with domain knowledge for multimodal medical image segmentation" (2025â€“2028).

October 2025

Published senior-authored journal article on ProtGram-DirectGCN ("Inferred global dense residue transition graphs from primary structure sequences enable protein interaction prediction via directed graph convolutional neural networks") in Frontiers in Bioinformatics.

June 2025

Published "Adapting a Segmentation Foundation Model for Medical Image Classification" in the Proceedings of the 38th IEEE International Symposium on Computer-Based Medical Systems (CBMS 2025).

Spring 2025

Awarded TWU Internal Research Grant ($5,000) as PI for HPC AI infrastructure upgrades; appointed to the Editorial Board of Research in Biomedical Engineering and Technology; and participated in TACCSTER 2025 at UT Austin.

2023 â€“ 2024 Milestones (Faculty & Lab Launch)

Fall 2024: Advised 5 M.Sc. graduate capstones in Health Informatics & Data Science at TWU; taught Foundations of Data Science and Fundamentals of Informatics; attended TACCSTER 2024 (Austin, TX), ISNA 2024, and ACM SIGCSE Early Research Scholars.

March 2024: Delivered invited oral presentation on MedGCN at MCBIOS 2024 (Atlanta, GA) and published two civic op-ed letters in the Denton Record-Chronicle (March 16â€“17 & March 30â€“31).

Spring 2024: Taught Data Warehousing, Statistical Programming, and Programming for Informatics at TWU; advised graduate capstone on ML models for Alzheimer's Disease progression; served on TWU AI Initiative, Sustainability, and Curriculum committees.

August 2023: Joined Texas Woman's University (TWU) as Assistant Professor of Computer Science; awarded $66,000 Startup Fund to establish the Data2AI4LifeSciences Lab and received The Hanover Grants Academy Award.

Summer 2023: Published essays on AI and spiritual philosophy in Illumination and AI Monks on Medium; volunteered with Dallas CASA.

Spring 2023: Served as Assistant Professor of Computer Science and Faculty Advisor for the CS Club at Southern Arkansas University (teaching Computer Science II, Database Management Systems, and Unix Operating Systems).

2017 â€“ 2022 Milestones (Postdoc, Ph.D. & UT Austin)

2022 â€“ 2023: Postdoctoral Research Associate at the University of North Texas (UNT) conducting NIH-funded Graph Neural Network research for drug repurposing with Dr. Serdar Bozdag, developing novel algorithms for identifying drug candidates for complex diseases, and contributing to NIH R01 grant proposals focused on graph representation learning; peer reviewer for Cambridge University Press Journal of Natural Language Engineering and IEEE BIBM.

May 2022: Graduated with Ph.D. in Computer & Information Science from UA Little Rock and honored as Outstanding Doctoral Graduate (2022); published MedGraph in Frontiers in Big Data, ModER in IJACSA, and ITNG 2022 (Springer).

2020 â€“ 2021: Earned M.Sc. in Computer & Information Science; co-authored the landmark PubMed Knowledge Graph in Nature Scientific Data (2020), COVID-19 literature networks in Scientometrics (2021), and computational social science research in Voluntas (2021); completed Data Science Research Internship at AbbVie Inc. (Urbana-Champaign, IL) conducting research on data-driven drug discovery via graph representation learning, and selected for the Data Science for Social Good Fellowship.

2017 â€“ 2020: Doctoral Researcher & Teaching Fellow at The University of Texas at Austin and the Texas Advanced Computing Center (TACC) (funded by Lockheed Martin and Intel), focused on developing algorithms for assessing cognitive load via eye tracking in high situational awareness environments; won the Best Short Paper Award at ACM SIGCHI ETRA 2019, UT Austin Professional Development Award (2019), and UT Austin Graduate Recruitment Fellowship (2017); served as Editorial Fellow at the Journal of Information & Culture (UT Press).

2005 â€“ 2017 Archive (Early Research & Industry)

January 2017: Travel to Miami for family engagements; completed Software Engineering Internship at Intel Corporation (Santa Clara, CA) working on Intel Graphics Performance Analyzers.

December 2016: Complete revamping and redesign of personal academic website.

November 2016: Participated in the Supercomputing 2016 (SC16) conference in Salt Lake City, UT.

2015 â€“ 2016: Researcher at the Emerging Analytics Center (EAC) developing immersive CAVE Virtual Reality applications, including CAVE Fluid Simulation, Endoscope SLAM, RealSense/Kinect 3D Reconstruction, EmotivVR, and Leap Motion Interfaces. Presented work at SIGGRAPH 2015, NVIDIA GDC, and ICAT; published XLPM / VisInt-X in IS&T Electronic Imaging (EI 2016) and MCBIOS.

2011 â€“ 2014: Software Developer at Arkansas.gov (NIC Inc.) building state e-government portals; served as a Graduate Assistant and earned a Professional M.Sc. in Information Technology from Arkansas Tech University (2013).

May 2011 â€“ Aug 2011: Software Delivery Consultant at WeDo Technologies (Cairo, Egypt), integrating RAID business and revenue assurance software.

Aug 2010 â€“ May 2011: Software Developer at Mobinil (France Telecom Egypt), developing Java web services on the webMethods platform for CRM and Billing system integration.

Jan 2009 â€“ Jul 2010: Software Developer at Xpress Integration, delivering telecom billing management systems across Tunis (Tunisie Telecom), Rabat (Maroc Telecom), and Cairo (Ericsson).

Jul 2008 â€“ Dec 2008: Maintenance Engineer for chemical lab instruments at Hanna Instruments in Cairo.

Aug 2003 â€“ Jul 2008: Earned B.Sc. in Electrical & Computer Engineering from Ain Shams University with a Distinctive Capstone Project Award for an Intersection Collision Avoidance System (ICAS) and passed the international NCEES Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination.

2007 â€“ 2008: Software Engineering Intern at Giza Systems in Cairo, Egypt.

Jul 2005 â€“ Sep 2005: Web Developer Intern at Vodafone Egypt, designing an internal C# timesheet web application.

sections.heading: Current Research
sections.content_html:
Current Research

Proteomics & GCN

ProtGram-DirectGCN

A novel method for protein-protein interaction (PPI) prediction using directed graph convolutional neural networks. This work infers global dense residue transition graphs directly from primary sequence tokens, bypassing computationally heavy 3D folding while achieving state-of-the-art predictive performance.

Read Publication (Frontiers 2025)
Neuro-Symbolic AI

Multimodal Biomedical AI

Investigating data quality, parameter scaling, and interpretability in biological foundation models. Integrating neuro-symbolic reasoning to resolve exponential parameter explosion while infusing physical chemical priors into biomedical discovery workflows.

sections.heading: Fatherhood & Family Life
sections.content_html:
Fatherhood & Family Life

Future aspirations of fatherhood, mentorship of youth, moral stewardship, and family bonds.

Core Life Aspiration

Beyond all academic titles, research accomplishments, and professional endeavors, I hold family life and the aspiration of fatherhood as one of life’s most sacred callings. Looking forward to the future, nurturing, guiding, and raising a family will stand at the very center of my life, informing the ethical perspective, patience, and devotion I bring to scholarship, education, and community stewardship.

I envision fatherhood as an active, daily practice of patience, unconditional love, mindful presence, and intellectual curiosity. Whether exploring nature on weekend hikes, discovering science and history together, reflecting on ethics and spirituality, or encouraging creative expression, sharing these moments of wonder with a future family will be an enduring source of joy, purpose, and balance.

Data Quality, Engineering & Natural Language Processing

Entity Resolution, NLP & Governance

TransER: Unsupervised Entity Resolution

KDD Draft

Transformational Embeddings for Data Quality

TransER introduces an unsupervised entity resolution approach via transformational embeddings, mitigating the quadratic complexity of traditional pairwise comparisons. It leverages graph neural network concepts and transformational embeddings analogous to TransE to automate data cleaning, curation, and integration without handcrafting syntactic rules.

Entity Resolution Unsupervised Learning Data Curation

MedGCN: Biomedical NER

MCBIOS 2024

Query-time Character Level Embedding via Bidirectional GCNs

A novel approach to Biomedical Named Entity Recognition (NER) that recasts the problem as a character-level representation of tokens in a directed graph. Trained via a Bidirectional Graph Convolutional Neural Network, MedGCN operates on the fly without the overhead or carbon footprint of fine-tuning large language models.

sections.content_html:
Islamic Jurisprudence & Legal Theory

Classical methodology, legal maxims (Qawa‘id Fiqhiyyah), objectives (Maqasid), and contemporary applied ethics.

Fiqh & Usul

My scholarly work in Islamic jurisprudence centers on the rigorous analytical frameworks of Usul al-Fiqh (principles and methodology of legal reasoning) and Maqasid al-Shariah (higher normative objectives of Islamic law). I approach jurisprudence not merely as a historical code of ordinances, but as a living, profoundly sophisticated intellectual epistemology rooted in textual hermeneutics, linguistic analysis, analogical reasoning (Qiyas), and public interest considerations (Maslahah).

A major focus of my inquiry is the application of classical juristic reasoning to modern dilemmas arising at the intersection of emerging technologies, data systems, and biomedical innovation. Drawing upon my dual expertise in algorithmic sciences and Islamic studies, I investigate the jurisprudential and moral accountability of autonomous systems, algorithmic bias as an ethical injury, privacy and data ownership as protected interests, and bioethical questions in genetic medicine and computational biology.

Legal Hermeneutics & Usul

Methodological inquiry into classical sources of jurisprudence, evidentiary standards, linguistic signification, and comparative schools of jurisprudence (Madhahib).

AI & Computational Bioethics

Formulating ethical boundaries and jurisprudential rulings on artificial intelligence, clinical decision algorithms, algorithmic agency, and biological data preservation.

Higher Objectives (Maqasid)

Preserving the core universal protections of faith, life, intellect, lineage, and property within modern socioeconomic systems and institutional governance.

Chronological Timeline of Islamic Scholars (Imams)

A comprehensive chronological timeline of the great Imams and scholars of Islamic jurisprudence up to 1000 AH, detailing their contributions, foundational texts, and methodological schools.

sections.heading: Psychological Inquiries & Cognitive Studies
sections.content_html:
Psychological Inquiries & Cognitive Studies

Cognitive ergonomics, human motivation, emotional regulation, and psychological well-being.

Interdisciplinary

Alongside my technical and jurisprudential work, I maintain an active, passionate inquiry into human psychology, behavioral dynamics, and cognitive sciences. This interest originally emerged from my academic research in human-computer interaction (HCI), eye-tracking methodologies, and cognitive load assessment, but has since expanded into deeper reflections on the architecture of the human mind, internal motivation, and emotional resilience.

My psychological investigations explore how individuals navigate decision-making under uncertainty, build cognitive habits, cultivate mental clarity, and process moral responsibility. Furthermore, I am deeply intrigued by the dialogue between classical spiritual psychologies—particularly the traditions of character refinement (Tazkiyah) and introspective self-accounting (Muhasabah)—and contemporary positive psychology, cognitive-behavioral insights, and emotional intelligence.

Cognitive Ergonomics & Attention Dynamics

Understanding how visual environments, information overload, and cognitive bandwidth shape human attention, memory retention, and mental exhaustion.

Character, Virtue & Moral Psychology

Examining how moral conviction, spiritual discipline, and psychological resilience interact to foster emotional balance and ethical leadership.

sections.content_html:
Expanding Circles of Service

My philosophy on integrating service into academic and intellectual life.

I view service not as an extracurricular obligation, but as an deeply integrated dimension of academic and intellectual life. Genuine impact emanates outward through concentric circles of influence. By beginning with those closest to us and expanding outward, we build sustainable, meaningful contributions at every level of society.

1

Class & Research Lab

Dedicating extended time to students through comprehensive office hours and organizing specialized research seminars to foster early inquiry.

2

Department

Participating actively in curriculum development committees and driving departmental recruitment efforts to ensure a robust academic pipeline.

3

Institution

Engaging in campus-wide sustainability initiatives and shaping institutional policy regarding the future of Artificial Intelligence in education.

4

Professional Network

Serving the broader academic community through rigorous peer-review processes, editorial board roles, and conference organization.

5

Home Community

Grounding intellectual work in local realities through active volunteerism, community outreach, and serving on faith organization committees.

6

National Level

Advocating for freedom of speech, academic inquiry, and peace. Crucially: advising on national security matters regarding the risks of AI, participating in cybersecurity initiatives, and collaborating constructively with government agencies.

7

Global & International

sections.heading: Lab Narrative
sections.content_html:
Lab Narrative

Our research ecosystem is dedicated to AI for Life Sciences, grounded in foundational theoretical computer science and applied data science. Our domains include Computer Vision, Language Modeling, Information Science, Network Science, and Human Factors. We advance traditional analyses by pioneering Graph Representation Learning and Multimodal Data Integration. These tools help us decode biological and cognitive systems, from the cell to the brain. Through rigorous Data Quality assessment and advanced Big Data mining, we transform unstructured information into dynamic Knowledge Graphs that support modern AI models. This integrated approach bridges the gap between data validity and model accuracy. These elements form the essential foundation of computational life sciences.

sections.content_html:
Mission

Our mission is to accelerate progress in Biomedical Informatics, Biomedical Literature Mining, Biomedical Imaging, and Computational Drug Discovery. We achieve this by developing novel Graph Neural Networks, integrating large foundation models, and Automating Knowledge-Extraction pipelines that transform raw data into actionable insights. To address structural challenges in Data Science, we establish rigorous standards for Data Quality, Entity Resolution, and Entity Recognition. This approach ensures our models are grounded in reliable data. We also enhance Human Factors in AI by integrating Biometrics and Non-Linear Analysis to model operator attention during system interaction. This aims at bridging the gap between machine logic and human cognition. Through this dual focus, we are committed to ethical, sustainable end-to-end AI systems that generate valid, interpretable, reliable, and safe scientific hypotheses.

Vision

We envision a future in which Data Mining, Network Biology, and Information Retrieval merge into an intelligent system that advances scientific discovery. In this world, Language Modeling and Graph Theory work together to automatically curate biological knowledge and reduce the time needed for discoveries. Here, AI is a transparent partner, always grounded in Ethics, Law, and Data Quality, and serves to enhance, never replace, human intelligence. Ultimately, we strive to define the next generation of Biomedical Intelligence, where structured networks clarify the underlying logic of life.

sections.content_html:
Live Interactive Product & Research Demo DATA_CURATION + VISUALIZATION_REPORTING IS&T Electronic Imaging / JIST

XLPM & VisInt-X: From Heavily Curated Tandem MS/MS Spectra to Multi-Scale 3D Structural Proteomics

Chemical Cross-Linking Mass Spectrometry (XL-MS) generates millions of noisy, combinatorial precursor and fragment ion spectra. XLPM (Cross-Linked Peptide Mapping) and VisInt-X exemplify the core Unity Systems engineering paradigm: pairing heavy upstream relational data curation with zero-install, multi-scale WebGL/D3 visual analytics.

STAGE 1 // UPSTREAM CURATION
15-Table Relational & Perl Engine

In-silico Trypsin (K/R) cleavage, PTM normalization, 5 ppm precursor / 0.8 Da b/y ion matching, 14N/15N isotopic shift filtering, and Target-Decoy FDR scoring.

STAGE 2 // 3-TIER D3 MATRIX
Hierarchical Visual Drill-Down

Drill seamlessly from the global tryptic peptide matrix (Level 1) to the MS/MS scan Treemap (Level 2) down to exact amino-acid cross-link sites (Level 3).

STAGE 3 // 3DMOL.JS WEBGL
Synchronized 3D PDB Inspection

Clicking Level 2/3 cells dynamically maps interacting peptide chains (Blue) and exact cross-linked residues (Red) onto dual 3D crystal structures.

Curated Pipeline Specifications

  • Relational Schema: xlpmwebv1 (15 MySQL Tables)
  • Precursor Tolerance: 5.0 ppm (Orbitrap MS1)
  • Fragment Tolerance: 0.8 Da (b/y Ion Series)
  • Isotopic Labeling: 14N / 15N Heavy-Light

Tryptic Peptide Sequence Grid

MS/MS Precursor Scan Distribution

Clicking a Level 1 cell minimizes the matrix and renders a D3 Treemap of all MS/MS precursor scans matching that peptide pair, sized by score.

Synchronizes with Level 2 & Level 3 selections to color interacting peptide chains in Blue and exact cross-linked amino acid residues in Red.

sections.heading: Research Program: Data2AI4LifeSciences Lab
sections.content_html:
Research Program: Data2AI4LifeSciences Lab

An interdisciplinary research ecosystem bridging theoretical AI with computational life sciences

Core Mission: Transforming noisy, unstructured biomedical data into high-fidelity dynamic Knowledge Graphs and trustworthy AI models—ensuring both mathematical validity and clinical reliability.

1. Data Quality in AI

  • Entity Resolution (ER): Linking non-unique records across disparate sources.
  • Hierarchical record clustering & modularity optimization.
  • Automated data quality assessment & observability pipelines.

2. AI in Life Sciences

  • Knowledge Graphs & GNNs: Harmonizing multi-omics with PubMed literature.
  • Computational drug discovery & automated hypothesis generation.
  • Directed Graph CNNs for protein-protein interaction prediction.

3. Human Factors in AI

  • Cognitive Modeling: Eye tracking, scanpaths & operator attention modeling.
  • Bridging machine logic with human expert cognition.
  • Ethical, sustainable, and transparent AI system design.
[Min 5-7] Frame the research program: While many researchers treat data as a black-box commodity, my lab focuses on the bedrock: Data Quality and Knowledge Graphs. When data is rigorously verified and structured symbolically, AI models become dramatically more interpretable, robust, and accurate.

Disambiguating and semantically querying millions of biomedical publications

The Challenge & Innovation

  • Biomedical Fragmentation: 35M+ PubMed papers lack unified semantic linkage between authors, clinical entities, and grants.
  • PubMed Knowledge Graph (PKG): Extracted entities using fine-tuned BERT; linked authors and NIH funding at massive scale.
  • MedGraph Architecture: Knowledge Graph Embeddings (TransE, RotatE) enabling conceptual search beyond simple keyword matching.

IJACSA (2022) & ITNG Springer (2022).

Direct Graph CNN Architecture

  • The Challenge: Experimental 3D protein structure determination is prohibitively slow; 1D sequence models miss spatial contact topology.
  • Our Method (2025): Developed an algorithm to infer Global Dense Residue Transition Graphs directly from primary amino acid sequences.
  • Directed GCNN: Captures directional residue constraints, achieving accurate protein-protein interaction (PPI) prediction without physical 3D coordinates.

Ebeid IA, Tang H, Gu P (2025). Inferred global dense residue transition graphs from primary structure sequences enable protein interaction prediction via directed graph convolutional neural networks.

sections.heading: Taming the AI Parameter Explosion
sections.content_html:
Personal Frontier Research

Taming the AI Parameter Explosion

A Neuro-Symbolic & Graph-Based paradigm to bypass brute-force parameter scaling

The Critical AI Scaling Crisis: The Unsustainable Trillion-Parameter Trap

Modern foundation models achieve performance through massive brute-force overparameterization (billions to trillions of weights). This incurs extreme computational costs, massive energy footprints, and uncontrollable black-box hallucination.

My Independent Research Initiative

(Conducted as personal fundamental research alongside student lab projects)

  • Structured Relational Knowledge: Replace memorization of facts in dense weights with sparse, dynamically queried Graph Neural Networks (GNNs).
  • Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning: Ground neural representations in formal symbolic logic constraints to eliminate hallucination.
  • Drastic Parameter Compression: Target equivalent or superior reasoning fidelity with orders of magnitude fewer parameters.

Long-Term Strategic Impact

  • Green & Sustainable AI: Enables high-capability AI on edge and local compute clusters without requiring multi-million-dollar GPU farms.
  • Verifiable Reasoning: Logic-guided graph traversals guarantee interpretability and safety in high-stakes domains.
  • Intellectual Leadership for Egypt: Establishes a unique, high-impact theoretical and algorithmic contribution originating from Nile University.
[Min 11-13] Present this personal frontier project: - Clarify that while my students work on translational biomedical AI (segmentation, proteomics, data engineering), this is my personal core passion project. - Modern AI is trapped in brute-force scaling: more parameters, more GPUs, more power. - My solution leverages Neuro-Symbolic AI and GNNs: structured knowledge graphs can represent concepts and relations symbolically, drastically shrinking parameter size while enhancing reasoning fidelity. - This positions Nile University at the forefront of post-scaling AI architectures.

Transforming students from passive learners into confident, research-ready computer scientists

2. Research-Teaching Synergy

  • The classroom as an incubator for future researchers.
  • Replace toy assignments with real open-source biomedical & graph datasets.
  • Expose students to genuine challenges in data quality and scalability.

3. Guild-Based Mentorship

  • Paired programming and collaborative code reviews.
  • HyFlex (Hybrid-Flexible) design ensuring equity for working/remote students.
  • Continuous low-stakes assessments to reinforce mastery and confidence.

sections.heading: Strategic Value Proposition for Nile University
sections.content_html:
Strategic Value Proposition for Nile University

Integrating research funding, curricular innovation, and administrative leadership at ITCS

1. Research & Funding Engine

External Grant Leadership

  • Establish the Data2AI4LifeSciences Lab at Nile University.
  • Translate US NSF PI track record into winning STDF, ASRT, and EU Horizon proposals.
  • Engage NU students in active international US-Egypt collaborative publications.
2. Curricular Excellence

Industry-Ready AI & CS

  • Deliver high-enrollment core CS/AI courses and graduate seminars with 4.5+ teaching rigor.
  • Bridge academic theory with industrial MLOps, Data Observability, and Bio-AI.
  • Train MSc/PhD theses aligned with Egypt's healthcare and tech sectors.
3. Institutional Builder

Accreditation & Governance

  • Contribute immediately to ABET / NAQAAE accreditation, curriculum review, and faculty recruitment.
  • Build R1/R2 international partnerships (UT System, TWU, UALR) and local industry consortia.
  • Advance Egypt Vision 2030 in AI sovereignty and digital transformation.

Long-Term Commitment: Finalizing permanent relocation to Egypt—bringing a proven blend of US federal grant leadership, evaluated teaching mastery, and proactive administrative citizenship to serve Nile University.

[Min 8:30 - 9:30] Strategic Alignment for the Dean & Provost: - Summarize the 3 concrete deliverables I bring to Nile University: 1. External grant generation (replicating my NSF success with STDF, ASRT, and international partners). 2. High-impact teaching and thesis supervision across AI, Data Science, and Bioinformatics. 3. Dedicated administrative service in accreditation, faculty recruitment, and university AI strategy.
